_about: Drafted by Claude on 2026-11-24 (E3, prompt 74) for Nav's approval; 'approved' stays null until Nav approves, and npm run check-leg refuses the leg until then. The Mars to Vesta leg's detours for the daily vote (the faster and steady options are shared, in content/vote-options.json). hours: how much later the arrival. Every fact checked against 'source' on 2026-11-24; 'quote' is the supporting text.

detours.label: Chase a Vestoid, a chip off Vesta: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Debris blasted off Vesta, from sand and gravel to boulders and small asteroids, is known as Vestoids.
detours.quote: ranging in size from sand and gravel to boulder and smaller asteroids (known as Vestoids)

detours.label: Study Vesta's dark patches: about 3 hours later
detours.fact: Vesta's dark material is thought to have been left there by other asteroids crashing into it.
detours.quote: the dark material is believed to have been deposited by other asteroids crashing into Vesta

detours.label: Measure Vesta's dusty blanket: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: Those crashes may have wrapped Vesta in a layer of material 1 to 2 metres thick.
detours.quote: wrap the Vesta in a blanket of material about three to seven feet (one to two meters) thick

detours.label: Scan Vesta for water-bearing rocks: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Vesta has little water of its own, so its water-bearing minerals probably came from somewhere else.
detours.quote: Vesta's composition is volatile-depleted, so these hydrated materials are likely exogenic.

detours.label: Look back at Earth's meteorite hunters: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: More than 50,000 meteorites have been found on Earth, and 99.8% of them come from asteroids.
detours.quote: More than 50,000 meteorites have been found on Earth. Of these, 99.8% come from asteroids.

detours.label: Look up the first ion-drive explorer: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: Ion engines like Dawn's were first proved on NASA's Deep Space 1 mission.
detours.quote: Ion propulsion was proved on NASA's Deep Space 1 mission

detours.label: Weigh our fuel against Dawn's: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: Dawn carried 425 kg of xenon fuel when it launched.
detours.quote: The Dawn spacecraft carried 425 kilograms (937 pounds) of xenon propellant at launch.

detours.label: Test the spare ion engine: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Dawn had three ion engines: two to last the whole mission, and a spare.
detours.quote: Two ion propulsion engines are required to provide enough thruster lifetime to complete the mission … the third engine serves as a spare

detours.label: Map the craters on Vesta: about 3 hours later
detours.fact: Dawn found Vesta heavily cratered, with rough ground somewhere between a planet's and an asteroid's.
detours.quote: Dawn found a heavily cratered surface on Vesta, with a rough topography that is transitional between planets and asteroids.

detours.label: Wave at Dawn's old path: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: NASA's Dawn launched on 27 September 2007 and went on to orbit both Vesta and Ceres.
detours.quote: Sept. 27, 2007 … giant asteroid Vesta and dwarf planet Ceres
